# lane

> lane is a command-line tool that runs every git worktree or project as an isolated dev stack at its own `*.localhost` URL — with no port conflicts. A shared Traefik proxy routes by hostname, so any number of stacks run side by side. You can bring up your whole stack, or just the services you changed and borrow the rest from a running base stack. It is built for both humans and AI coding agents to test in parallel and ship faster.

Key facts:

- **What it is:** a single static Go binary (CLI), no runtime dependencies.
- **Platforms:** Linux, macOS, Windows.
- **Requirements:** Docker (>= 28) with Compose (>= 2.20), git; Tilt only for Tilt projects.
- **How it works:** stacks publish zero host ports; a shared proxy routes `<slug>.localhost` to the right stack. Each git worktree gets its own slug, so N worktrees run as N live stacks simultaneously.
- **Selective bring-up:** `lane up <service>` runs only the named services (deps auto-included); `-p/--profile` activates Docker Compose profiles. Plain `lane up` brings up the whole stack.
- **Auto-routing:** every HTTP service is reachable at `<slug>-<service>.localhost` automatically (no explicit route config required).
- **Base-borrowing:** `lane up <service> --base` runs the changed services fresh and borrows everything else from a running base stack of the same project — instead of booting a full copy per worktree.
- **Agent loop:** `lane up --wait --json` (race-safe, machine-readable; reports per-service `running` status) → run tests against the returned URL → `lane down`.
- **License:** MIT. Source: https://github.com/Dheeraj-Nalapat/lane

## Docs

- [Home](https://dheeraj-nalapat.github.io/lane/): overview of lane and what it does.
- [Install](https://dheeraj-nalapat.github.io/lane/install/): install via prebuilt binary, install script, `go install`, or from source.
- [Getting started](https://dheeraj-nalapat.github.io/lane/getting-started/): onboard a project and bring up your first stack in ~10 minutes.
- [Selecting & reaching services](https://dheeraj-nalapat.github.io/lane/selecting-services/): bring up a subset of services or a compose profile; reach each at `<slug>-<service>.localhost`.
- [Borrowing from a base stack](https://dheeraj-nalapat.github.io/lane/base-stacks/): run only changed services fresh and borrow the rest from a running base stack with `lane up --base`.
- [Using lane with coding agents](https://dheeraj-nalapat.github.io/lane/agents/): run Claude Code / Cursor agents in parallel, one isolated stack per worktree.
- [Command reference](https://dheeraj-nalapat.github.io/lane/commands/): every command, flag, JSON output, and exit code.
- [HTTPS](https://dheeraj-nalapat.github.io/lane/https/): optional trusted HTTPS for `*.localhost` via mkcert.

## Recipes

- [Plain docker-compose project](https://dheeraj-nalapat.github.io/lane/recipes/compose/): the most common case — no Tiltfile or shim required.
- [Tilt project](https://dheeraj-nalapat.github.io/lane/recipes/tilt/): drive Tilt with live-reload and the Tilt dashboard.
- [Frontend dev server with HMR](https://dheeraj-nalapat.github.io/lane/recipes/frontend-hmr/): run Vite / Next.js dev servers with hot-reload behind the proxy.
